translationRepairs: Early in the Wude era he sent envoys to submit to the court and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Ba, receiving generous reassurance.
Early in the Wude era he sent envoys to submit to the court and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Baque, receiving generous reassurance.
The appointed title is 吐烏過拔闕可汗; 'Tuwuoguo Ba' omits 闕, and restoring it as Baque matches the Chinese without changing the rest of the sentence.
At the beginning of Wude he sent envoys to submit inwardly and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Ba; he was treated with generous reassurance.
At the beginning of Wude he sent envoys to submit inwardly and was appointed Qaghan Tuwuoguo Baque; he was treated with generous reassurance.
The same truncated title appears in the literal line; 吐烏過拔闕可汗 includes 闕, which 'Tuwuoguo Baque' restores.

Qaghan Jieli resented China's marriage alliance with him and repeatedly sent troops to raid; he also sent word to Tongyehu, saying, "If you welcome a Tang princess, you must pass through my territory."

Qaghan Jieli resented China's marriage alliance with Tongyehu and repeatedly sent troops to raid; he also sent word to Tongyehu, saying, "If you welcome a Tang princess, you must pass through my territory."
與之和親 refers to China's marriage alliance with Tongyehu, the partner of the surrounding 和親 narrative; after the subject 頡利可汗, 'with him' wrongly suggests Jieli was the marriage partner.
Eastward the Ili River was the boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tokhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, Shiguo of the Shi, Heguo, Muguo, and Kangguo, all were under his command.
Eastward the Ili River was the boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tokhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, the Shi state, Heguo, Muguo, and Kangguo, all were under his command.
The list is 石國、史國, two distinct states; 'Shiguo of the Shi' garbles 史國, while 'the Shi state' matches the Chinese and the idiomatic line.

Shidianmi had followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; with an army of one hundred thousand he pacified the Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan, and was called the Ten Surname Tribes, ruling their people for generations.

Shidianmi had followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; with an army of one hundred thousand he pacified the Hu states of the Western Regions and set himself up as qaghan; his people were called the Ten Surname Tribes, and his line ruled them for generations.
號十姓部落，世統其眾 names the people the Ten Surname Tribes and says his line ruled them for generations; the original English wrongly applies that name to Shidianmi himself.

At first Shidianmi followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; he had an army of one hundred thousand men, went to pacify the various Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan, and was called the Ten Surname Tribes, ruling their masses for generations.

At first Shidianmi followed the chanyu in commanding the ten great chieftains; he had an army of one hundred thousand men, went to pacify the various Hu states of the Western Regions, set himself up as qaghan; his people were called the Ten Surname Tribes, and his line ruled their masses for generations.

The original wrongly makes Shidianmi himself 'called the Ten Surname Tribes', but the proposed brackets are editorial scaffolding, not finished English; the revision states that the people were so called and that his line ruled them.
His clansman Buzhen wished to set himself up as qaghan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishe's younger brothers and nephews.
His elder clan brother Buzhen wished to set himself up as qaghan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishe's younger brothers and nephews.
族兄 is an elder brother of the same clan; 'clansman' drops the seniority the Chinese states.
He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Qaghan Xingxiwang, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
襲父興昔亡可汗 is the inherited title Xingxiwang; 'Khan Irbis She' does not render 興昔亡可汗.
He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Qaghan Xingxiwang, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
The literal line repeats the same false title; 興昔亡可汗 is Qaghan Xingxiwang, not Khan Irbis She.
Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Ashina Mochuo and Wuzhile.
Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Mochuo and Wuzhile.
The Chinese names only 默啜; the literal 'Ashina Mochuo' invents a clan name absent from this sentence, while the idiomatic line already has Mochuo.
Ashina Bozhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
Ashina Buzhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
阿史那步真 is Buzhen (步); 'Bozhen' is a wrong romanization that splits him from the same man elsewhere in the chapter.
Ashina Bozhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
Ashina Buzhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
The literal line has the same false 'Bozhen' for 步真; Buzhen is the accurate romanization.

Together with Mishshe he helped subdue Helu and was further appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

Together with Mishe he helped subdue Helu and was further appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
與彌射 is Mishe; 'Mishshe' is a misspelling of that name.

Together with Mishshe he helped subdue Helu and was additionally appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

Together with Mishe he helped subdue Helu and was additionally appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
The literal line repeats the misspelling 'Mishshe' for 彌射; Mishe is correct.

His son Husero, who in his own realm had been Bolu She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

His son Husiluo, who in his own realm had been Buli She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
斛瑟羅 and 步利設 are Husiluo and Buli She; 'Husero' and 'Bolu She' are inaccurate romanizations that obscure the same person and title used elsewhere.
Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husero in migration to the interior. The Ashina line of the Western Turks thus came to an end.
Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husiluo in migration to the interior. The Ashina line of the Western Turks thus came to an end.
隨斛瑟羅 is the same Husiluo as in neighboring units; 'Husero' is a false variant of that name.

His son Husero, who in his own realm had been Bolu She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

His son Husiluo, who in his own realm had been Buli She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
The literal line has the same wrong Husero/Bolu She for 斛瑟羅 and 步利設; Husiluo and Buli She match the Chinese.
Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husero, migrating to settle within the interior. The Ashina clan of the Western Turks thus came to an end.
Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husiluo, migrating to settle within the interior. The Ashina clan of the Western Turks thus came to an end.
The literal line again renders 斛瑟羅 as Husero; Husiluo is the correct romanization of that name.
At that time Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi; the princess sent a yabgu officer bearing one thousand horses to Anxi for mutual trade.
At that time Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi; the princess sent a headquarters officer bearing one thousand horses to Anxi for mutual trade.
牙官 is an officer of the headquarters/tent (牙), not a yabgu (葉護); 'headquarters officer' restores the Chinese office.
